newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-THREE-WAY OPEN TIE FOR LEAD WITH NINE HOLES TO PLAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THREE-WAY OPEN TIE FOR LEAD WITH NINE HOLES TO PLAY.

text.p: Tom Lehman, Colin Montgomerie and Jeff Maggert were tied for the lead, one shot ahead of Ernie Els, with nine holes to play Sunday in the U.S. Open golf championship.

The leading trio were locked at four under par, with 1994 Open champion Els at three-under as the quartet, playing in the last two groups of the day, waged a tense battle along the sprawling Congressional Country Club course.
There was one four-way tie, two different three-way ties and three different individual leaders during the tumultuous front nine.
Lehman began the round with a two-shot lead at five under par on a sunny day with a fresh breeze blowing.
He parred the first two holes before taking successive bogeys at the third and fourth that started the see-saw struggle for the lead.
Maggert jumped into the lead on the fourth hole when he sank a long birdie putt to produce a two-shot swing as Lehman bogeyed his second successive hole after finding the thick, greenside rough.
Lehman nearly holed out from the fairway at the next hole to tie Maggert for the lead at four-under.
Montgomerie, the first-round leader, birdied the first hole to move to three under, and he and Els stayed within a stroke of the lead for most of the front side.

Then birdies by both Montgomerie and Els at the par-3 seventh -- just moments ahead of bogeys taken by both Lehman and Maggert at the long and difficult par-4 sixth -- created a four-way tie for the lead at three-under.
Els birdied the eighth hole to temporarily take sole possession of the lead. Lehman and Maggert followed with birdies of their own at number eight for another three-way tie.
Els and Montgomerie traded places in the pecking order on the next hole when the South African bogeyed after landing in the greenside rough while the Briton birdied.

The only other player getting into the red numbers on the leaderboard was Jay Haas, who birdied two of the first three holes to reach two under par. A double bogey at the fifth dropped him back to level par before a ninth-hole birdie made him one-under at the turn.
The Grand Slam aspirations of Masters champion Tiger Woods officially ended Sunday as he posted a two-over 72 to finish at six-over 286.
Woods still managed some shots that thrilled the crowd, most noticeably a spectacular approach shot at the 16th that drew applause from spectator President Clinton and his daughter, Chelsea.
